bullets.title: Bird by Bird: Some Instructions on Writing and Life
bullets.creator: Anne Lamott
bullets.note: convertkit-mail2.com/c/xmumv0zqqa6hnnknq/gwfnh5hdvpdx8k/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9BTk5FTEFNT1RU)**)**. If you plan on any creative undertaking, whether business, writing, or art, I strongly recommend this book. If you spend a lot of time working alone and get trapped in your head, it’s required reading. It saved my sanity and has done the same for several friends who’ve gone from “I want to quit” to New York Times bestsellers.

bullets.title: Katharine McCormick
bullets.note: Katharine McCormick (August 27, 1875 – December 28, 1967) was a U.S. suffragist, philanthropist, and, after her husband's death, heir to a substantial part of the McCormick family fortune. She graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1904, earning a BSc in biology. She funded most of the research necessary to develop the first birth control pill, which the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the sale of in 1957 for menstrual disorders and added contraception to its indications in 1960. In sum, she provided roughly $2 million ($23 million today) of her own money for the development of the contraceptive pill. She was [inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame](https://el2.convertkit-mail2.com/c/xmumv0zqqa6hnnknq/82aqhoh0490k6o/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud29tZW5vZnRoZWhhbGwub3JnL2luZHVjdGVlL2thdGhhcmluZS1kZXh0ZXItbWNjb3JtaWNrLw==) in 1998 for her “significant impact on women’s equality in the areas of suffrage, contraception, and scientific education.”
